Root reachability is fine (all states reachable_from_initial=true), so no derived reachability contract is needed. The concrete behavioral consequence is that the three orthogonal-region "concurrent activation" obligation (NL3-ACTION-1, must_progress) fails because each region's leaf (junction2, junction3, InitialState after junction4) has zero outgoing transitions -- deterministically confirmed by LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostics and refuted deadlock verify checks -- so the state cannot sustain ongoing/continuous concurrent operation as NL3 requires. This is routed to V1(initial_scope) per the deadlock-frontier rule for an explicit progress/continuation obligation on an operating state whose regions have no continuation. The trigger_set (NL2-TRIGGERSET-1) is a single combined event trigger, not three separate literal triggers, giving a mismatch candidate (predicate S3, triggers input). The guard_disjointness derived contract (NL2-DERIVED) is also affected: since the trigger set uses one combined event string rather than three independently distinguishable events, the alternatives cannot be operationally distinguished by the model - preserved as predicate-null W1. Termination-state contract is not present (no termination_state role established in this contract set), so no termination candidate is emitted. Event-consumer coverage contract is satisfied (single declared consumer reachable), so omitted. Endpoint (NL2-ENDPOINT-1) is satisfied: DetectingState->junction1->ActiveState realizes the transition to active mode, so omitted. The cardinality contract's owner is bound at the model level to ActiveState; no separate exact author source_id row distinct from the state's own source_id 'ActiveState' exists in exact_source_inventory.states, so owner_source_id is set to that same value 'ActiveState' to satisfy the both-or-neither pairing rule while owner_model_ref carries the corresponding closed ModelIR ref.

decisions.reason: NL3 requires continuous/ongoing concurrent control activation per region. The complete FCSTM inventory and diagnostics (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING for junction2, junction3, InitialState) show three of the four region chains terminate at leaves with zero outgoing transitions, establishing that the continuous-activation reading is not sustained past that point. However, a competent alternative reading remains: reaching a quiescent leaf could represent the region's control simply remaining engaged/steady (a one-shot activation satisfying a weaker 'capability' reading of NL3) rather than a liveness violation, since NL3's text ('allow for concurrent activation') is structurally satisfied by the existence of the BrakeControlState/SteeringControlState/SensorControlState activation edges themselves. No frozen predicate exists to decide between the ongoing-liveness reading and the structural-capability reading, so both remain compatible with the supplied facts.
decisions.violated_obligation: Each orthogonal region of ActiveState (Brake, Steering, Sensor) must sustain ongoing/continuous concurrent activation while ActiveState is active.

decisions.basis: S3 predicate plan and fcstm_model:S3 receipt with counterexample, canonical source tr_0002.
decisions.reason: S3 predicate executed with an exact counterexample: expected trigger set {collision with pedestrian detected, possible frontend collision detected, rear-end collision detected} vs observed single combined trigger 'Frontend_Collision_or_Rear_end_Collision_or_Collision_with_Pedestrian_detected'. The formal trigger_set cardinality is 1, not 3, a clear mismatch established by a completed, supported native predicate. The proposed rebuttal (single compound event as author intent equivalent) is contradicted by the exact typed S3 semantics requiring trigger-set equality to three distinct tokens, and pyfcstm's native event identity treats the combined string as one atomic trigger with no decomposition; the supplied facts exclude the rebuttal.
decisions.violated_obligation: The activation transition (DetectingState->junction1) must be triggered by exactly three distinct named events.

decisions.basis: Exact transition:line:14 fact, target junction3 outgoing-refs empty, no NL terminal/completion clause supplied for this specific candidate.
decisions.reason: The exact transition fact shows zero triggers/guard into a leaf with no outgoing transitions, consistent with a missing-trigger defect. The predicate is null (no frozen check for trigger-presence-as-completion-vs-defect), and the dossier does not supply enough to decide between 'missing required trigger' and 'intentional completion transition'.
decisions.violated_obligation: The lifecycle transition SteeringControlState->junction3 must remain event-controlled rather than an untriggered completion edge.

decisions.basis: transition:line:22 single combined trigger fact, guard=null, transition_groups ALT-NL2-1/2/3 hints, absence of guard-disjointness predicate.

This is a competent design-choice reading supported by the exact modeling-formalism constraint.

The complete FCSTM inventory and deterministic diagnostics show three of the region chains dead-end at leaves with no outgoing transitions, which is a distinct semantic property from mere endpoint or declaration existence and cannot be represented by any S/G/V frozen predicate for state_action beyond the strict entry/phase/action triple (which is absent here), so this remains a predicate-null W1 candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The region leaves are reachable and each region did execute one control-activation transition (BrakeControlState->junction2, etc.), which may satisfy a one-shot 'activation' reading rather than a continuous progress obligation; NL3 could be read as describing structural capability rather than an ongoing liveness requirement.
issues.title: Orthogonal regions of ActiveState terminate at dead-end leaves, undermining continuous concurrent control activation

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions (transition:line:22 triggers=[Frontend_Collision_or_Rear_end_Collision_or_Collision_with_Pedestrian_detected]); exact_source_inventory.transitions tr_0002 event field; NL2 contract normative_statement requiring three named events.
issues.expected: The activation transition (DetectingState->junction1) must be triggered by exactly three distinct named events: frontend collision detected, rear-end collision detected, collision with pedestrian detected.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM transition transition:line:22 (DetectingState->junction1) has triggers=['Frontend_Collision_or_Rear_end_Collision_or_Collision_with_Pedestrian_detected'], a single combined event name rather than three separately declared/triggerable events; the source inventory likewise declares only one combined event string 'Frontend Collision or Rear-end Collision or Collision with Pedestrian detected' (tr_0002).
issues.reason: The NL contract requires the activation transition's trigger set to equal exactly three distinct named detection events, but the closed model and canonical source both encode a single combined event name as the sole trigger, a formal mismatch in trigger-set cardinality/identity.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The single event name textually encodes all three conditions via natural-language disjunction, and pyfcstm treats it as one atomic trigger; a reviewer could argue the modeler intended it as a semantically equivalent single compound event rather than three formally distinguishable triggers, so the trigger-set property may be considered satisfied at the level of author intent even though the formal trigger_set has cardinality one instead of three.
issues.title: Activation transition triggered by one combined event rather than three distinct named triggers

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING for junction2/line5, junction3/line7, InitialState/line10); verify_facts.non_proved deadlock checks refuted for junction2/junction3/InitialState with outgoing_count=0; reference_inspection_facts diagnostic_counts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF=3.
issues.expected: While ActiveState is active, each of its concurrent regions must sustain ongoing/continuous concurrent activation of its collision-avoidance control (brake, steering, sensor) as an explicitly continuous operating obligation.
issues.observed: Deterministic inspection facts show LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostics for state:junction2:line:5 (BrakeControlState region), state:junction3:line:7 (SteeringControlState region), and state:InitialState:line:10 (SensorControlState region's terminal chain junction4->InitialState); verify_facts confirms these as refuted deadlock checks with outgoing_count=0 for junction2, junction3, and InitialState. All three concurrent regions reach a reachable non-final leaf with zero outgoing transitions, so none of the three collision-avoidance controls can continue operating/concurrently activate after reaching its region's terminal leaf.
issues.reason: NL3 establishes an explicit continuous/concurrent operating obligation for ActiveState's three orthogonal regions; the deterministic deadlock-frontier facts show each region terminates at a reachable leaf with no outgoing transition, which is the closest available deterministic evidence that the required ongoing concurrent activation is not retained.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A reviewer could argue that reaching a quiescent leaf state within an orthogonal region is itself a valid steady 'active' control state (e.g., brake control simply stays engaged) rather than a deadlock, so the absence of an outgoing transition does not necessarily violate the NL's continuous-activation obligation if the leaf state itself represents sustained control action; the frozen predicate registry also has no dedicated ongoing-concurrency check, so this remains W1 rather than a definitively proven violation.
issues.title: Concurrent regions of ActiveState reach frontier leaves with no outgoing continuation, failing the ongoing concurrent-activation obligation

issues.basis: transition_groups NL-GROUP-NL2-ACTIVATION alternatives ALT-NL2-1/2/3 each carrying a distinct 'event' hint; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions transition:line:22 shows a single combined trigger and guard=null.
issues.expected: The three named activation alternatives (frontend collision, rear-end collision, collision with pedestrian detected) from DetectingState must remain distinguishable/mutually exclusive triggers driving the same activation transition.
issues.observed: The closed model has only a single transition (transition:line:22, DetectingState->junction1) with a single combined trigger name and no guard; there is no exact per-event distinguishability -- all three NL alternatives are operationally collapsed into one indistinguishable event with no separate guard/trigger identity.
issues.reason: The transition-group's three alternatives share one source and target but the closed model realizes them as one combined trigger with no guard, so the three alternatives cannot be operationally distinguished from each other; this is a guard/trigger distinguishability property with no frozen predicate expressing compound-event decomposition, so it is preserved as predicate-null W1.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Because pyfcstm/FCSTM has no native support for compound OR-events split into three distinguishable triggers on one edge, the single combined-name modeling could be considered the closest faithful encoding of an OR-condition rather than a genuine guard-disjointness defect; no distinguishing guard was ever required by NL beyond triggering activation.
issues.title: Three activation alternatives collapse into one indistinguishable trigger instead of three mutually exclusive detection events

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination. The closed FCSTM shows ActiveState is entered via junction1->ActiveState but ActiveState itself (as a composite pseudo-terminal target for the whole sub-machine) has no outgoing transition at its own scope, and its three concurrent regions each terminate in a leaf with no outgoing transition (junction2, junction3, InitialState), which are deterministically flagged LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/W_DEADLOCK_LEAF. The single declared event is consumed only by DetectingState before activation; no consumer exists for events after entering ActiveState, which is consistent with NL2's consumer-coverage contract already covering DetectingState (declared==reachable), so NL-CONTRACT-NL2-CONSUMER-1 is satisfied per inspection facts (reachable_consumer_state_refs equals declared consumer). Root reachability is fine (all states reachable_from_initial=true), so no derived reachability contract is needed. The concrete behavioral consequence is that the three orthogonal-region "concurrent activation" obligation (NL3-ACTION-1, must_progress) fails because each region's leaf (junction2, junction3, InitialState after junction4) has zero outgoing transitions -- deterministically confirmed by LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostics and refuted deadlock verify checks -- so the state cannot sustain ongoing/continuous concurrent operation as NL3 requires. This is routed to V1(initial_scope) per the deadlock-frontier rule for an explicit progress/continuation obligation on an operating state whose regions have no continuation. The trigger_set (NL2-TRIGGERSET-1) is a single combined event trigger, not three separate literal triggers, giving a mismatch candidate (predicate S3, triggers input). The guard_disjointness derived contract (NL2-DERIVED) is also affected: since the trigger set uses one combined event string rather than three independently distinguishable events, the alternatives cannot be operationally distinguished by the model - preserved as predicate-null W1. Termination-state contract is not present (no termination_state role established in this contract set), so no termination candidate is emitted. Event-consumer coverage contract is satisfied (single declared consumer reachable), so omitted. Endpoint (NL2-ENDPOINT-1) is satisfied: DetectingState->junction1->ActiveState realizes the transition to active mode, so omitted. The cardinality contract's owner is bound at the model level to ActiveState; no separate exact author source_id row distinct from the state's own source_id 'ActiveState' exists in exact_source_inventory.states, so owner_source_id is set to that same value 'ActiveState' to satisfy the both-or-neither pairing rule while owner_model_ref carries the corresponding closed ModelIR ref.
